heading: Changelog
introBefore: A record of the features, fixes, and adjustments in each release. Version numbers follow three-part semantic versioning (

PATCH.name: Patch version
PATCH.desc: Bug fixes and minor tweaks that don't change external behavior

4_4_0.title: Editor experience overhaul: Notion-style code blocks, block dragging, equation editing
4_4_0.summary: A round of polish across the writing editor — code blocks, math equations, block manipulation, the slash menu, and the side panels are all brought in line with Notion / mainstream note apps, plus a batch of fixes for everyday editing annoyances.

changes.0: Notion-style code blocks: automatic syntax highlighting (37 common languages, with light/dark token palettes), a searchable language picker, and one-click copy; inside a block Tab indents and Shift+Tab outdents (multi-line aware) instead of escaping the block.
changes.1: Block drag handle (⠿): hovering a block reveals a handle on the left to reorder by dragging, or open a menu to duplicate / delete the whole block — also fixing the long-standing trouble of deleting code, math, and table blocks.
changes.2: Revamped equation editing: a larger rendered preview with the input box docked right beneath it (Notion-style); pressing Enter renders and the caret continues naturally; LaTeX pasted with outer delimiters (\[ \], $$, $) such as matrices now renders instead of erroring.
changes.3: Slash command fixes: the menu now appears the instant you type / (no need to nudge the caret); choosing any command no longer leaves the keyword you typed behind (e.g. /heading → H3 yields an empty heading, not stray text).
changes.4: Cleaner figure/table lists: figures or tables without a caption (e.g. a scanned approval page) are no longer numbered or added to the list of figures/tables — no more skipped numbers or blank entries; this matches the final PDF / LaTeX export.
changes.5: Side panels & interaction details: long text in the AI rewrite original, the smart-citation search box, and export format descriptions now wraps/scrolls instead of overflowing; the drop indicator line clears immediately after a drag; moving a sentence or block no longer pops the rewrite/cite toolbar by mistake.

4_3_0.title: Upload tracking dashboard: failures no longer vanish
4_3_0.summary: Adds an upload audit system that fixes the blind spot where a failed paper upload left no trace of which file or what error. Every upload (success/failure/cache hit) now leaves a persistent record; on failure the maintainer is emailed automatically and the original file is kept for download to reproduce the problem locally; a daily upload summary email is also sent. The /admin page is token-protected.

changes.0: Upload audit trail + admin page: a new /admin dashboard lists every upload's time, filename, status, failed stage and error. The records are independent of the History list — failed papers don't appear in History but are always queryable here. Gated by an ADMIN_TOKEN (disabled when unset).
changes.1: Instant failure email + daily summary: when an upload's analysis fails, the maintainer is emailed immediately (filename, failed stage, error) — no need to be watching; a daily digest of the day's uploads is also sent. Both optional — skipped silently when SMTP isn't configured.
changes.2: Failed originals kept for download: previously a failed paper's file became an orphan on disk and its error lived only in memory (lost on restart). Now failed files are retained and downloadable from the admin page to reproduce the issue locally.

4_2_1.title: Fix the un-dismissable "new version" update banner
4_2_1.summary: On browsers that had installed the tablet app or visited before, the service worker also cached the /version check endpoint; after a deploy the new page kept comparing against a stale version number, so the update banner reappeared immediately even after clicking refresh. The service worker now only caches immutable static assets — version checks always hit the network.

changes.0: Service worker no longer caches /version or other dynamic requests (cache-first is limited to hashed static assets and icons), and the cache name was bumped so existing devices purge the stale entry; the update banner now appears once, only when a new version is really live, and goes away after refresh.

4_2_0.title: One-click thesis PDF, Taiwan thesis template, tablet app, and stability fixes
4_2_0.summary: Export pipeline upgrade: compile editor documents straight to a thesis PDF (server-side XeLaTeX with CJK support out of the box), plus a new template matching Taiwan degree-thesis conventions; the frontend now installs as a standalone tablet app. Also fixes two stability issues: CJK/filename problems in LaTeX export, and analysis failures on very long papers with large appendices.

changes.0: One-click thesis PDF: choosing PDF on export compiles via server-side XeLaTeX — no local TeX install needed; Chinese (CJK) works out of the box.
changes.1: Taiwan degree-thesis template: a new LaTeX layout matching local thesis conventions (cover page, watermark position, line spacing, margins), with layout settings made global across all export formats.
changes.2: Tablet app (PWA): the frontend can be installed via "Add to Home Screen" and opens standalone full-screen on tablets, with no browser chrome.
changes.3: LaTeX export hardening: fixes CJK compile failures and cross-origin downloads losing the filename (CORS now exposes it).
changes.4: Long-paper analysis fix: papers with large appendices/references could blow past the model's output-token cap during EDU segmentation and fail the whole upload ('OpenAI returned invalid JSON'). Overlong sections are now chunked automatically, halved on truncation, and the error message is human-readable.

4_1_0.title: Differentiation moat: citation traffic-light verification, defect checking, semantic RAG
4_1_0.summary: On top of Jenni parity, this adds capabilities others don't have — bringing correctness into the act of writing via a neuro-symbolic engine and RAG. Verify whether a cited source actually supports your claim (🟢/🟡/🔴 + the supporting sentence); run the 13 REL rules over the whole draft for structural defects with inline marks; re-rank citation search by semantic similarity (with a shown %); and click a citation to fetch the cited paper's full text and surface the sentences that best support you.

changes.0: Citation traffic-light verification: in the recommend list and on inserted references, one click checks whether a source actually supports your claim → 🟢 supports / 🟡 partial / 🔴 unsupported, surfacing the supporting sentence and reason (an LLM judges from the abstract, not just keywords).
changes.1: Defect check at writing time: a toolbar action runs the 13 REL rules over the draft (claims without evidence, methods without motivation, misaligned conclusions…), lists defects in a side panel, marks them inline with red/amber/blue wavy underlines, and jumps to the sentence. The existing paper-review engine, wired into writing — something Jenni can't do.
changes.2: Semantic citation ranking: search candidates are re-ordered by semantic similarity between your claim and each abstract (OpenAI embeddings), beating raw keyword relevance; each candidate shows a 'semantic %'.
changes.3: Full-text grounding: 'Find supporting text' on an inserted citation fetches the cited paper's open-access full text (arXiv etc.), splits it into sentences, and surfaces the ones that best support your claim with a similarity % (falls back to the abstract); full-text vectors are cached locally for instant repeat.

4_0_0.title: New “Writing Editor”: draft a paper from scratch — Jenni-AI parity plus Notion/Heptabase-style block editing
4_0_0.summary: This release expands the product from “analyze an existing PDF” to “write a paper from scratch” with a standalone /editor mode: a TipTap v3 rich-text editor, document management with version history, AI sentence autocomplete (ghost text), highlight-to-rewrite, outline generation, OpenAlex-backed smart citations (six styles, dual full-text+DOI links, one-click link refresh), and DOCX/LaTeX/HTML export. It adds Notion/Heptabase-style structured block editing: a “/” slash menu to swap blocks, Markdown shortcuts, image upload with an auto List of Figures, KaTeX math, and tables with an auto List of Tables plus an add/remove row-column toolbar.

changes.0: New Writing Editor mode: a standalone /editor with a document list, autosave, and version history; powered by TipTap v3 (ProseMirror) rich text.
changes.1: AI Autocomplete (ghost text): grey inline continuation at the cursor, Tab to accept; now uses smart boundary triggering (only at word/sentence ends, ~1s pause) plus ⌘/Ctrl+J to request one manually, with an auto/manual/off toolbar toggle.
changes.2: AI rewrite menu: select text → paraphrase / simplify / expand / shorten / improve fluency / academic tone / fix grammar, or a custom instruction; streamed preview to accept, retry, or discard.
changes.3: Outline generation: apply the standard IMRaD structure, or enter a topic and let AI generate a tailored heading tree, inserted in one click.
changes.4: Smart Citation: select a sentence or keywords → search real papers via OpenAlex → insert a citation; references offer dual “full text + DOI” links (avoiding dead mirrors, preferring trusted sources) with one-click refresh of all links.
changes.5: Multiple citation styles: APA / MLA / Chicago / Harvard / IEEE / numeric, switchable instantly across in-text markers, references, and export.
changes.6: Export: DOCX / LaTeX / HTML with in-text citations and a reference list (LaTeX uses ctex for CJK).
changes.7: Slash menu and Markdown shortcuts: type “/” for a block menu (heading / list / quote / code / divider / image / math / table…), with live Markdown conversion (##, -, >, …).
changes.8: Images and math: image upload + caption + an auto List of Figures; KaTeX math (inline $..$ and block), click to edit the LaTeX.
changes.9: Tables: insert an editable table with a numbered caption above and an auto List of Tables; a toolbar appears in-table to add/remove rows & columns, toggle the header, or delete the table; columns are resizable and wide tables scroll inside their frame.
changes.10: Quality fixes: autocomplete no longer echoes repeated preceding text; citation “full text” links now scan locations for trusted sources (arXiv/PMC…) instead of dead mirrors; wide tables scroll horizontally inside the editor instead of breaking the layout.

3_8_0.title: Multilingual UI and dark mode: 繁中 / English switching, light/dark theme
3_8_0.summary: The whole interface gains Traditional Chinese and English, switched via URL prefixes (/zh-Hant, /en) and remembered across visits, with new visitors following the browser language automatically. A dark-mode toggle is added: the choice is remembered via cookie, follows the OS light/dark preference on first visit, and never flashes on reload. LLM-generated defect descriptions and suggestions are now produced bilingually, and the paper assistant replies in the current UI language.

changes.0: Multilingual UI (Traditional Chinese / English): built on next-intl, switched via the URL prefixes /zh-Hant and /en, with a language switcher added to the header; the choice is stored in a cookie, and new visitors have their browser language auto-detected. Locale is a data dimension, so adding languages later requires no structural changes.
changes.1: Dark mode: a light/dark toggle is added to the header and the choice is remembered via cookie; the theme is rendered server-side from the cookie so reloads never flash, and the first visit follows the system prefers-color-scheme; the knowledge-graph mini-map's nodes, edges, and zoom controls switch with the theme too.
changes.2: Bilingual content: defect descriptions and suggestions are produced in both Chinese and English at analysis time (batch-translated with a lightweight model), so switching languages shows them instantly; the paper assistant reads context and replies in the current UI language.
changes.3: Fixed early dark-mode issues: flash on reload, a light-gray halo around the page, and the knowledge-graph mini-map's invisible nodes and white-on-dark zoom controls.

3_7_0.title: Interface polish and the analysis-waiting experience: global task tracking, mobile-first, consistent across pages
3_7_0.summary: The overall interface is tighter and more professional: the header keeps only the logo and version, the report-oriented system guide is hidden, filler text and decorative emoji are removed, and a shared PageHeader gives every page the same title height and format. The upload page becomes a mobile-first single-column focused design (drag-and-drop upload, large buttons, mobile hamburger menu), with the rules explanation moved to the rule statistics page. Long-running analysis gains global task tracking: switching tabs no longer loses progress, completion fires a browser notification plus a tab-title flash plus a header pill, and leaving the upload page asks for confirmation first. The KG defect cards also gain a human-rating mechanism.

changes.0: Interface polish: the header now shows the logo plus a version badge (the text wordmark is removed), the nav hides "System guide" (/about is still reachable directly), and pages like about/changelog drop decorative emoji and excess gray text and use larger type, for a tighter overall look.
changes.1: Mobile-first upload-page redesign: switched to a single-column focused drag-and-drop upload card, with larger buttons and tap targets and the big blank area fixed; added a <sm mobile hamburger menu. The original "13 REL rules" explanation panel moved to the rule statistics page to keep the upload screen clean.
changes.2: Global analysis-task tracking: post-upload polling and progress are promoted to a global Context, so switching tabs or reloading no longer loses progress; completion triggers a browser notification (under secure contexts) plus a tab-title flash plus an "Analysis complete" header pill, so users can leave to do something else and come back.
changes.3: Navigation guard and preference persistence: leaving the upload page while analysis is running asks for confirmation first (no nagging if you're already on another page), and closing the tab shows a beforeunload warning; the completion pill auto-closes after a few minutes of inactivity; notification preferences are stored in the browser.
changes.4: Consistent page titles: added a shared PageHeader component to unify the height, type size, and layout of every page's title.
changes.5: Human rating added to KG defect cards: the "defects involving this passage" card on the knowledge-graph FRU layer gains correct / partial / wrong annotation, sharing the same judgment API and statistics as the results page.
changes.6: Fixed the completion notification re-firing endlessly (polling didn't stop after completion) and the navigation guard mis-firing on non-upload pages; when a PDF can't be parsed it now degrades gracefully to a card (reload / download the original file) instead of showing a bare red error.

3_6_0.title: Major knowledge-graph page redesign: section-grouped cards, defect linkage, in-place source locating
3_6_0.summary: The Entity and FRU layers move from force-directed graphs to card views grouped by section; clicking shows details in the focus panel on the right, and any source sentence in the focus panel can open a right-side drawer in place to jump to the corresponding position in the PDF and highlight it, without leaving the graph page. At the same time, leftover "v3" wording in the interface is removed and a simple new app icon is added.

changes.0: Entity layer: the force-directed graph becomes collapsible cards grouped by section (Abstract → … → Uncategorized) with type filtering; clicking an entity shows a 1-hop relationship mini-graph (incoming | entity | outgoing) and evidence sentences in the focus panel. Entities with no relationships are assigned a representative section by name-matching against the full EDU text (uncategorized dropped from 83 → 5).
changes.1: FRU layer: the sequence flow chart becomes section-grouped cards plus function filtering; clicking an FRU shows the summary, the EDU source text it covers, and the defects involving that passage (linked via fru.edu_ids ∩ defect.evidence_edu_ids).
changes.2: In-place source locating: a locate button is added next to each source sentence in the focus panel; clicking it embeds the PDF in a wide right-side drawer on the same page, auto-scrolls to the page containing that sentence, and highlights it, without leaving the graph page.
changes.3: Removed leftover "v3" wording from the interface (tab title / about / README / backend FastAPI title), and added a simple "document + checkmark" app icon used in the header.

3_5_0.title: Removed the Phase 2 few-shot feedback loop in favor of purely manual evaluation
3_5_0.summary: Removed the feedback loop where "once a rule accumulated ≥3 judgments they were injected into the prompt as few-shot examples." The reviewer's manual judgments (correct / partial / wrong) are kept, but used only to quantify precision and export ground truth—they are no longer written back into the prompt. Every check is now an independent zero-shot run, so results are reproducible.

changes.0: Removed few-shot injection: rules.check_rule no longer reads the past-judgments examples_block, the checker prompt drops {examples_block}, and db.get_judgment_examples and rules._build_examples_block are deleted. Rule checking is always zero-shot.
changes.1: Manual review mechanism retained: defect annotation (✅ correct / 🤔 partial / ❌ wrong), per-rule soft precision statistics, judgments export (ground truth), and the eval summary all remain unchanged.
changes.2: The stats page removes the "Phase 2" column and the few-shot / zero-shot explanation; section 8 of the about page changes from "Phase 2 feedback loop" to "Manual evaluation mechanism," removing the feedback-loop sequence diagram and the in-context learning literature entry.

3_4_0.title: Automatic paper-title detection
3_4_0.summary: You no longer have to enter the title by hand when uploading: the system uses an LLM to read the real title from the paper's first page, so you can leave it blank (fill it in manually if you want to override).

changes.0: Automatic title detection: after extraction, gpt-5.4-mini reads roughly the first 1500 characters of the paper's first page to obtain the title (one very lightweight call with negligible cost), applied automatically when the user leaves the title blank, falling back to the filename only if detection fails.
changes.1: The title field in the upload form becomes an optional override, with the hint "Leave blank to auto-detect."

3_3_0.title: Major analysis performance optimization: parallelization + rule slimming
3_3_0.summary: Section extraction and the 13 rule checks now run in parallel, and rule-verdict output is trimmed, bringing a full analysis from about 9 minutes down to about 2 minutes with a corresponding cost drop; verdicts match the old version (verified with a fixed-graph A/B across 4 papers with no regression).

changes.0: Analysis pipeline parallelized: section extraction (EDU/ER/RST·FRU) and the 13 REL rules are now dispatched simultaneously via a thread pool (OPENAI_MAX_WORKERS, default 6), bringing full processing time from about 9 minutes → about 2 minutes (about 5×), with order-preserving, reproducible results.
changes.1: Rule-verdict output slimmed: the verdict schema fills detail fields only when there is a violation, so non-violations no longer produce throwaway text; rule_check output tokens drop by about −43% and time by about −35%.
changes.2: Added unit tests (garble detection / extraction routing / singleton concurrency) and a thread-safe singleton; docs trimmed to three core files—SYSTEM / DB_SCHEMA / TODO—with performance notes added.

3_2_0.title: Automatic new-version detection and update prompt
3_2_0.summary: An already-open tab sitting on an outdated frontend will automatically detect a new deployment and show an update banner, preventing users from staying on an old version.

changes.0: Added a /version endpoint and a frontend version watcher: it compares the bundle's built-in version against the server's currently deployed version, and when a mismatch is detected shows a non-dismissible update banner at the bottom of the screen; clicking "Update now" reloads.
changes.1: Version-check timing: it checks immediately when the tab regains focus (focus / visibilitychange), and otherwise polls once every 60 seconds.

3_1_0.title: PDF OCR fault tolerance and the changelog page
3_1_0.summary: Solves the problem where some LaTeX papers (Type 3 fonts without a ToUnicode CMap) copy out as garbage, causing LLM extraction to fail.

changes.0: Added PDF garble detection + tesseract OCR fallback (chi_tra + eng): if native extraction detects glyph-cipher garbage, it automatically falls back to OCR to recover the text, while preserving each text segment's page number and bbox coordinates.
changes.1: PDF text extraction moved to a background task, so OCR (about 3–5 minutes for 30 pages) no longer blocks the upload's HTTP request.
changes.2: Added real-time progress hints: "Parsing PDF…" → on detecting garbage, switches to "PDF font can't be read directly; recognizing via OCR (about 3-5 minutes)."
changes.3: Added a "Changelog" page defining the three-part semantic versioning scheme.
changes.4: Fixed the garble-detection threshold: the original two-condition check ("real-character ratio + noise ratio") missed substitution-cipher garble (letters shifted to other letters, so the letter ratio stays high); it now looks only at the ratio of noise characters such as backticks/asterisks being > 3%.
changes.5: The backend Docker image installs tesseract-ocr and the chi-tra / chi-sim / eng language packs, and sets TESSDATA_PREFIX.

3_0_0.title: System baseline: Knowledge Graph + LLM paper review
3_0_0.summary: Automatically finds structural defects in academic papers using a four-layer EDU/Entity/RST/FRU structure + a Neo4j KG + 13 REL rules.

changes.0: Extracts the four-layer EDU / Entity / RST / FRU structure from a paper and writes it into a Neo4j Knowledge Graph.
changes.1: 13 REL rule checks (Cypher finds candidates + LLM interprets), outputting logical defects and revision suggestions.
changes.2: Human-as-judge annotation interface (per-defect correct/wrong/partial) + Phase 2 few-shot feedback loop.
changes.3: KG visualization, rule statistics, PDF source-alignment view, SQLite persistence, and token/cost logging.
